memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "If the disease breaks out all over their skin and, so far as the priest can see, it covers all the skin of the affected person from head to foot, the priest is to examine them, and if the disease has covered their whole body, he shall pronounce them clean. Since it has all turned white, they are clean." - Lev 13:12-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Read that twice, because it seems backwards. A spot makes you unclean. Covering your entire body from head to foot makes you clean.

How can total infection be better than partial?

We should be careful not to build a doctrine on a puzzling verse. But we can observe what the text plainly says: the person who was partly affected was excluded, and the person who was wholly affected — with nothing hidden, nothing left to spread to, the whole condition fully visible — was pronounced clean.

There is something here that resonates deeply with the gospel. The people Jesus struggled to reach were never those who knew they were in a bad state. It was the respectable ones, the ones with only a spot, who could not receive Him. When the Pharisees complained about the company He kept, He answered: it is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick (Mark 2:17).

The tax collector in the temple would not even raise his eyes. God, have mercy on me, a sinner. And Jesus said that man went home justified before God, not the man who could list his virtues (Luke 18:13-14).

Half-admissions leave us outside. It is complete honesty about our condition that opens the door to grace.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you offering God a partial admission or complete honesty?
2. Does your respectability ever get in the way of your need for mercy?
3. What would praying like the tax collector look like for you today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I stop pretending that I am only slightly in need. I come to You honestly, as I truly am, and I ask for the mercy that only Jesus can give. Amen.
